items.title: 333 Tor exit nodes hijacked to intercept SSH traffic and retrieve plaintext email
items.content: Unknown hackers hijacked more than 300 Tor exit nodes and reconfigured them to favor unencrypted email traffic and redirect SSH connections through servers they controlled, a researcher reported Tuesday. The hijacking began in late August, when, according to Tor volunteers, the attacker used a valid password that had been reused to gain access to a Tor management server. The attacker then installed Ebury, a backdoor written for Linux that was discovered 12 years ago. Mysteries remain Then the attacker connected from the management server to a second Tor server, called Switzerland2, through SSH, using an RSA key that, for unknown reasons, investigators couldn’t find among Switzerland2’s authorized keys. With administrative control of Switzerland2, the attackers installed Ebury there as well. Finally, the attacker reconfigured settings on two exit nodes that Switzerland2 hosted.Read full article Comments

all_items.content: When a venture-backed startup goes a few years without raising a new round, it’s common to presume its odds of a sizable exit have gone down as well. This year, a number of larger acquisitions of private companies involved startups that haven’t disclosed a new investment for more than four years. Several of these acquisitions are quite recent — and in some cases, quite large. The standout is Uber’s purchase earlier this month of ezCater, a platform for catering and workplace meals, for $2.3 billion in cash. The deal comes nearly five years after Boston-based ezCater raised its last reported venture funding round. That’s not the only one. Many companies that raised during that time had difficulty attracting fresh capital or were reluctant to close new rounds at reduced valuations. Even with the more recent AI boom, little went to this cohort. Moreover, since the 2021 boom-era rounds were quite large, funded startups commonly had the option to cut operating costs and extend their runways with existing capital.
